text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: SEV=P1 — GPU pool exhaustion in us-west-2 (gpu-pool-3). Autoscaler failing to add nodes, accept/queue growth, increased 5xxs for some Dedicated customers. Paging oncall.laura_ops.
laura_ops: I’m on it. seeing queue depth jump on the metrics page now, +1200 queued reqs across pool-3. autoscaler events show repeated ProvisionFailed with quota checks.
mike_infra: copying. I can force a scale until we figure root cause — how many GPUs can we burst to from vendor?
ashley_prod: customers reporting slow tail latencies and 429/503s. Probably related to the v3.14.1 rollout that went out ~20m ago. We saw context-length knob increase for some routes.
deepak_sre: Confirming correlation: model v3.14.1 turned on extended_context by default for chat-rerank routes. KV cache per-session jumped ~3–4x on warmup. That increased per-GPU memory and decreased simultaneous concurrency.
carla_support: Ticket queue: 6 enterprise customers with errors, one in legal impacted. Escalated to CSMs.
laura_ops: okay mitigation plan: (1) force-scale pool to +6 GPUs (temp), (2) throttle/disable extended_context for rollout via feature-flag, (3) if needed rollback v3.14.1 to v3.13.9. Doing (1) now.
mike_infra: issuing manual scale: 
```
# manual scale command
infractl gpu scale --pool gpu-pool-3 --target-nodes 18 --reason "P1 autoscale failure"
```
mike_infra: scale submitted, vendor accepted 6 nodes, provisioning started. ETA ~3m for nodes to be ready.
laura_ops: watching queues... initial drop in per-host queued tasks as new nodes join but still high. Autoscaler logs say "scale inhibited: cooldown" and a repeated error: "InsufficientAccountQuotas: GPU quota exceeded" earlier — vendor quota spiking then recovering.
deeprak_sre: (typo) deepak_sre: also seeing that our autoscale controller is hitting a backoff loop because the model launch creates many warmup requests that look like load, the controller thinks cluster is hot and stops scaling further due to maxPoolSize limit.
ashley_prod: so two contributing things: vendor quota oscillation + higher per-request memory from larger KV caches.
carla_support: Customer impact: 6 enterprises had >10% request failures for 12–18m window, estimated MTTI to restore service ~30m unless rollback.
laura_ops: applying feature flag rollback now to cut extended context size -> reduce KV per-session. 
```
# feature flag toggle
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.local/toggles/extended_context -d '{"value":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
laura_ops: flag toggled. Observed immediate reduction in average KV size in metrics (from 2.8GB -> 0.6GB per host warmup). Queue depth trending down.
mike_infra: vendor nodes are healthy and joined, but autoscaler still refuses to scale beyond pool max (20). Current cluster = 18/20. If queues spike again we need to raise pool max or rollback.
deepak_sre: recommend short-term: keep manual scale, keep feature flag off, and set autoscaler maxPoolSize += 10 and reduce cooldown to 45s to allow quicker reaction once warmups settle. I'll prepare a patch.
laura_ops: agreed. Applying autoscaler override now.
```
# autoscaler patch (applied)
kubectl -n infra patch configmap autoscaler-config -p '{"data":{"maxPoolSize":"30","cooldownSeconds":"45"}}'
```
mike_infra: patch applied. We'll watch for flapping.
carla_support: CSMs notified, drafting customer update: short outage due to model rollout causing memory and autoscale feedback loops. No data loss. ETA recovery: now +10m.
laura_ops: queue depth back to near-normal after flag toggle and manual nodes, 503 rate dropping. Keeping manual scale until autoscaler stabilizes for 30m.
deepak_sre: root cause notes for postmortem: model v3.14.1 increased default context-window on certain routes, KV-cache per-session ballooned, warmup traffic during rollout looked like sustained load and tripped autoscaler heuristics, vendor quota oscillation prevented autoscaler from getting consistent capacity, autoscaler backoff logic plus conservative maxPoolSize caused insufficient headroom.
ashley_prod: action items: (A) rollback v3.14.1 gated rollout and revert default extended_context in model config (owner: product/ashley_prod), (B) autoscaler code: add warmup-detection signal to avoid conflating rollout warmup with organic load (owner: eng-runtime/mike_infra), (C) infra: coordinate with vendor to raise soft quota and faster provisioning (owner: infra/mike_infra), (D) add SLA customer notifications template (owner: support/carla_support).
carla_support: I’ll send interim customer note: apology + impact summary + mitigation done + follow-up postmortem pending.
laura_ops: handoff in 30m to night shift. Mike, Deepak will you take watch after I go offline?
mike_infra: I’ll take infra watch.
deepak_sre: I’ll own postmortem and RCA. Set me as postmortem owner.
laura_ops: recording timeline:
- 1749999999 incident-bot page (initial alert)
- +02m v3.14.1 rollout correlation observed
- +08m manual scale requested (added +6 GPUs)
- +12m feature-flag toggle to disable extended_context
- +18m queue depth returned to acceptable range, 503 rates dropping
- +25m autoscaler config adjusted (maxPoolSize, cooldown)
- +30m handoff prep and customer comms
laura_ops: leaving oncall in 30m — handoff notes in #oncall-logs. Postmortem owner deepak_sre.
incident-bot: Incident P1 CLOSED -> mitigated (manual scale + flag toggle + autoscale patch).
carla_support: customers notified, follow-up tickets created.
deepak_sre: will kick off a full postmortem doc with timelines, metrics, and change list. Preliminary mitigation summary attached here and will include a regression test for model rollout that simulates KV growth.
mike_infra: follow-up: we should have an autoscaler quick-toggle to temporarily relax pool limits during rollouts; filing infra ticket.
nashley_prod: also will pause the rest of the v3.14.1 rollout until we validate extended_context memory footprint per-route.
laura_ops: thanks all. leaving notes in thread, tagging folks: @mike_infra @deepak_sre @carla_support for follow-ups.
carla_support: ack.
laura_ops: handoff complete.
